name: Discerning Solitary Salticid
subject: Biology
headline: A tiny spider may remember who it has met.
hook: A tiny loner spider may remember who it has met.
found: Jumping spiders told a familiar spider from a stranger.
matters: Big social smarts can fit in a very small brain.

drawing.subject: a cute jumping spider (Salticidae) with its two huge shiny front eyes, fuzzy round body and short legs, looking up curiously as if it recognizes a friend
drawing.scene: Background: the sunny edge of a garden leaf and a stone wall where jumping spiders hunt, softly out of focus.

name: Babbling Sac-winged Pup
subject: Biology
headline: Baby bats may benefit from more than a song playlist.
hook: Baby bats babble, just like human babies.
found: Pups with more involved mothers practiced longer and sounded more grown-up.
matters: Learning to talk may lean on caring parents in many animals.

drawing.subject: a cute baby bat pup hanging upside down from a branch, mouth open mid-babble, with two or three small curved sound lines coming from its mouth
drawing.scene: Background: the inside of a cave roost at dusk with its mother and other bats hanging in soft shadow behind.

name: Facilitative Weed-clipping Pika
subject: Biology
headline: A yak’s best friend might be a tiny gardener.
hook: Pika, called pests, may be a yak’s best friend.
found: Yaks gained more weight where some pika lived, because pika clip a poisonous plant.
matters: Wiping out a “pest” can backfire on the animals we care about.

drawing.subject: a cute pika (a small round-eared mountain mammal, like a tiny tailless rabbit) holding a clipped sprig of a poisonous purple-flowered plant in its mouth
drawing.scene: Background: a high grassy alpine meadow of the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau with rocks, short grass and a yak grazing far away.

name: Synesthetic Pupillary Seven
subject: Psychology
headline: A gray number can make an eye react to color.
hook: For some people, a gray number looks colored.
found: Their pupils reacted to the color they experienced, though the screen stayed gray.
matters: The colors are real enough that the body responds to them.

drawing.subject: a cute gray number 7 character that glows warm orange around its edges, showing how a person with synesthesia sees a color in a gray number, with one big round curious eye beside it whose pupil is wide
drawing.scene: Background: a calm lab table with a computer screen showing gray numbers, like a perception experiment.

name: Statistical Neonatal Listener
subject: Psychology
headline: A newborn’s brain is already listening for the pattern.
hook: Babies just days old already notice sound patterns.
found: Their brains tracked repeats in syllables and in voices, even when the other kept changing.
matters: We may be born with a pattern finder that helps us learn to talk.

drawing.subject: a cute sleeping newborn baby wearing a soft blue EEG cap with small round electrodes, with gentle sound waves reaching its ear
drawing.scene: Background: a cozy hospital nursery with a crib and a soft monitor showing brain-wave lines.
